subject.title: [Feature]: models.providers.*.enabled flag to disable providers without removing config

question: Should OpenClaw add a public `models.providers.<id>.enabled?: boolean` contract, and what should happen when a disabled provider is selected as the primary or appears in fallbacks?
rationale: Source inspection proves the requested capability is missing, but the repository policy treats new config/default surfaces and provider fallback behavior as compatibility-sensitive product decisions.

options.title: Approve Shared Provider Eligibility
options.body: Add the public flag with one shared eligibility helper across config/schema, models.json generation, fallback, catalog/status, docs, and tests, including disabled-primary semantics.

options.title: Reject Provider-Level Disable
options.body: Keep the current operator model where disabling a provider means removing the provider block or editing default/fallback model references.

options.title: Defer To Provider Lifecycle Design
options.body: Hold this until provider enable/disable, setup, auth/status, model picker, and plugin lifecycle behavior are designed together.

recommendation.title: Approve Shared Provider Eligibility
recommendation.body: Add the public flag with one shared eligibility helper across config/schema, models.json generation, fallback, catalog/status, docs, and tests, including disabled-primary semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses the model config, fallback, status, docs, and provider-routing surfaces where steipete has the strongest feature-history and prior issue-context signal.
